options.plan: Staging only; organization offer documented, production entitlement unverified
options.region: No WorkOS region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Primary AuthKit staging; first-party organizations; active memberships; app-owned tenant access; no Connect or SCIM

conditions: Model customer workspaces as WorkOS Organizations in one staging environment, with explicit active memberships and application-owned resource authorization. Organization count is not unlimited API usage, capacity, account entitlement or a cost guarantee.

Per https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments, staging is testing-only, not customer-facing production. Keys, users, organizations and connections are environment-specific; production requires separate setup and billing review. The AuthKit allowance at https://workos.com/pricing is not free production SSO or Directory Sync.

Primary AuthKit organization context does not inherit Connect OIDC/SPA claims, Directory Sync SCIM, controls or residency. No account or live acceptance was verified; mutable Cloud evidence is dated, not release-pinned.

evidence.summary: The guide models B2B workspaces with Organizations and memberships. Proposed SUPPORTED is conditional staging application context, not a production entitlement or proven resource isolation.

conditions: Use organization-specific invitations for partner collaboration, with trusted organization mapping and application-side inviter authorization. An application-wide invitation without an organization is not a partner membership.

Consumer-domain organization invitations require the exact invited address; corporate-domain invitations can be accepted by another address on the same domain. Do not assume exact-recipient approval; review admission policy and verify the accepting user and intended organization server-side.

A portal business-admin role is not WorkOS workspace administration, an unrestricted API key or AuthWeave catalog-curator authority. Keep management credentials confidential and scoped. No emails, invitations, privileged API writes or live portal acceptance were performed.

evidence.summary: Organization invitations support collaboration with explicit acceptance and domain-specific recipient rules. Proposed SUPPORTED retains application admission and authorization prerequisites, not automatic exact-recipient approval or admin delegation.

conditions: The selected organization appears in org_id when applicable. Bind the validated user and organization to the requested resource tenant; reject missing, unknown or mismatched organization context where tenant access is required. Login selection, branding and email domain are not authorization.

Switching via refresh with organization_id requires an authorized session; handle failures without retaining the previous tenant's permissions. The application must validate tokens and current resource permissions on requests; organization claims do not prove database isolation.

Reconcile the guide's HTTP JWKS example and issuer spelling with the HTTPS/client-specific reference at https://workos.com/docs/reference/authkit/session-tokens before approval. Do not borrow Connect keys or token semantics. Tenant-switch negative tests, cached tokens and local-session enforcement remain unverified.

evidence.summary: AuthKit sessions carry selected organization context and support authorized organization switching. Proposed SUPPORTED requires application resource checks and reconciliation of guide/reference details; no live tenant isolation was tested.

conditions: Bind the stable environment-scoped WorkOS user_id to each organization_id membership; zero, one or many memberships are documented. Do not use email alone as membership authority or infer linked identities across connections or staging/production environments.

Require active membership for resource access; pending invitations and inactive memberships are not active access. Listing defaults to active memberships, so audit reads must request statuses and pagination deliberately rather than assuming completeness.

Create can reactivate an inactive membership; reactivate retains prior roles. Explicit authorization and role review are required, not a harmless read or retry. Deactivation has documented WorkOS session effects, but cached JWTs and application sessions need separate enforcement tests: https://workos.com/docs/authkit/users-organizations.

No membership mutation, identity linking, offboarding latency or SCIM/Directory Provisioning bridge was verified. Native membership management is not evidence of protocol, group transport or authentication-control availability.

evidence.summary: The canonical membership reference represents multiple user-to-organization relationships and explicit status/lifecycle operations. Proposed SUPPORTED concerns application membership context, not verified provisioning, session enforcement or identity linking.
